title: Is the steering signature robust to paraphrase? Testing non-identifiability practically

original_idea.body: Construct two behaviorally-equivalent steering vectors (CAA and null-space-perturbed) and compare their OOD divergence to test non-identifiability practically.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain to silent monitor failure under OOD, but the threat relies on a fairly abstract theory result.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Null-space-perturbed vector construction matched on in-distribution behavior needs solid ML/linear-algebra fundamentals.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused experiment but constructing matched equivalent vectors is a nontrivial setup dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Empirical companion to a theory result, public model, no internal access; externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on one model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The empirical OOD-divergence test of non-identifiable equivalent vectors appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Empirically testing whether behaviorally-equivalent steering vectors diverge OOD is an underexplored angle.
